fields.Dropoff: Contact the supplier or manufacturer. In most cases, they will take the tank back at no cost. If the supplier refuses to accept the tank, call (206) 296-4692. You will need to request approval to bring the tank to a household hazardous waste facility .

fields.Garbage: Ceiling tiles that don't contain asbestos can go in the garbage: Items must fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Dropoff: Bring acoustic ceiling tiles that don't contain asbestos to city transfer stations . Fees apply.
fields.Hazardous: If you believe the ceiling tile contains asbestos, contact the Puget Sound Clean Air Agency at (206) 343-8800.

fields.General: While the steel cans are recyclable, aerosol cans are hard to recycle because the contents are under pressure and can be a safety hazard at the recycle sorting facility. You need to know if your can has Hazardous or non-Hazardous material before you can dispose of it.
fields.Recycling: Empty aerosol cans that had non-hazardous materials in them can be put in the recycling ONLY if the can is completely emptied of contents and pressure.
fields.Garbage: Empty hazardous material aerosol cans. Partially full cans with non-hazardous content.
fields.Hazardous: Bring cans that contain hazardous materials like paint, solvents, bear spray, or other flammables to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee. Hazardous products are usually labeled with the words Danger, Poison, Caution, or Warning.
fields.Didyouknow: Spray sunscreen is considered a hazardous material due to its potential to harm both the environment and humans if inhaled. Dispose of partially full cans by dropping them off at a household hazardous waste facility. Completely empty cans can be put in the garbage.

fields.General: Watch Ask Evelyn Live for more information regarding proper disposal of these products.
fields.Donate: Donate air conditioners, heat pumps, or dehumidifiers in good condition to local thrift stores . Call first to determine acceptance policies. Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Garbage: Air purifier filters and furnace filters should be individually bagged and put in the garbage.
fields.Curbside: Call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000 to request special item pickup . Fees apply.
fields.Transferstation: Bring damaged air conditioners, heat pumps, and dehumidifiers to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check the rates page .

fields.General: Batteries are NOT allowed in the garbage, see below for disposal guidance and rules Household batteries include rechargeable, button batteries, and rechargeable batteries for power tools. See photo examples below. Follow these links for Vehicle Batteries , Embedded Batteries , or E-Mobility Batteries .
fields.Curbside: Each SPU Account Holder gets 1 free household battery pickup a year. To schedule your free pickup, you must call (206) 684-3000 to schedule your free pickup. Submit a request online or call (206) 684-3000 to schedule a pickup from your residence. The materials collected will be reclaimed and recycled. Fees apply to additional pickups.
fields.Transferstation: Household batteries can be dropped off at city transfer stations to be safely reclaimed and recycled with no fee Remove batteries from devices Tape each end of the battery
fields.Dropoff: The Battery Network is a free take-back program for rechargeable batteries. You can find free drop off locations on their locator tool.
fields.Hazardous: Damaged or recalled batteries are NOT accepted at city transfer stations. Take any damaged, bulging, or recalled batteries to a household hazardous waste facility . Batteries cannot go in the garbage because they contain chemicals that are harmful to people, animals, and the environment. Learn more about the city of Seattle's Ban on Batteries and Electronics in Garbage .

fields.Recycling: Metal parts larger than 3 inches go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Metal items with plastic, wood, or rubber attached Metal items that are smaller than 3 inches
fields.Dropoff: All metal, except car parts, are accepted as recycling at city transfer stations . There is no charge for recycling at the transfer station. Maximum size is 8 feet long. There is a charge for appliances, limit 2 per load.
fields.Binside: Large metal parts can be put at the curb for pickup on your recycling collection day. These must be bundled or tied. The maximum size is 2 feet on all sides.

fields.Recycling: Clean and dry aluminum foil should be balled up and larger than 3 inches Aluminum food pans Foil and trays must be empty, clean, and dry
fields.Garbage: Dirty or food-covered aluminum foil or food pans Wine bottle foil

fields.Hazardous: Call the Seattle Police Firing Range at (206) 684-7470 to dispose of ammunition or firearms.

Antifreeze is harmful to people, animals, and the environment and should never be poured down drains, toilets, or on the ground. Bring antifreeze to a household hazardous waste facility : All containers must be 5-gallons or less. Limit 50-gallons per trip.
fields.Didyouknow: Antifreeze is harmful to people, animals, and the environment and should never be poured down drains, toilets, or on the ground.

fields.Hazardous: Asbestos is considered a hazardous material that does not belong in the garbage. Because asbestos is harmful to people, animals, and the environment, it must be disposed of at designated facilities. Please bring any asbestos to an asbestos disposal facility near you.
fields.Didyouknow: Because asbestos is harmful to people, animals, and the environment, it must be disposed of at designated facilities.

fields.Recycling: Empty milk, juice, and soup cartons Cartons labeled Tetra Pak Other aseptic cartons Plastic spouts don't need to be removed to recycle Tetra Pak cartons. Caps should be removed and placed in the garbage.
fields.Garbage: Plastic and foil juice and squeeze boxes go in the garbage. Put plastic straws and caps in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Aspectic cartons are paper cartons lined with plastic. The plastic is removed and the paper fiber is recycled.

fields.Garbage: Asphalt roofing that doesn't contain asbestos can go in the garbage: Items must fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits p for your Garbage cart.
fields.Dropoff: Bring asphalt roofing shingles that don't contain asbestos to city transfer stations . Fees apply.
fields.Hazardous: If you believe the roofing contains asbestos, contact the Puget Sound Clean Air Agency at (206) 343-8800.

fields.Garbage: Broken auto and window glass can go in the garbage: Glass must fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits for your cart. Auto and Window glass are a different type of glass than bottles and jars, and cannot be recycled
fields.Dropoff: Bring auto glass to city transfer stations . Fees apply.

fields.Donate: Donate baking trays or cookie sheets in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give them away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Recycling: Baking trays and cookie sheets less than two feet in any direction and free of food residue go in the recycling.

fields.Garbage: Plastic and dirty metal drums that held non-hazardous material can go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Bring barrels and drums that held non-hazardous material to city transfer stations : Empty barrels and drums must be clean and cut in half. Clean metal can be recycled for no fee.
fields.Hazardous: Sealed drums and drums that held hazardous waste must go to King County Household Hazardous Waste .

fields.Donate: Donate bed frames in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Recycling: Metal bed frames can go in recycling. Rusted metal can be recycled unless the metal is falling apart. Small amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber can be attached. Be careful not to exceed the weight limits on your cart.
fields.Garbage: Metal items with large amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber attached. Metal items that are smaller than 3 inches.
fields.Curbside: Submit a request online or call (206) 684-3000 to schedule a pickup. Fee applies.
fields.Transferstation: Bring bed frames to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check the rates page .

fields.Donate: Donate things in good condition to thrift stores or organizations who accept textiles. Even stained, worn out, ripped, or damaged bedding, linens, towels, decorative pillows and other fabrics can be donated to thrift stores and turned into new products through Threadcycle . Some local thrift and second-hand stores are partners and will accept these items at their regular collection or drop box locations.
fields.Garbage: Bedding, linens, towels, down feathers, foam pads, and other fabrics can go in the garbage. Non-decorative pillows cannot be donated for Threadcycle and go in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Beverage cans: Empty soda and beverage cans go in the recycling. Crushed aluminum cans are ok to recycle. Food cans: Soup and other food cans are recyclable when they are empty, clean and dry. Keep can lids partially attached or push the lid into the can. You don't need to remove the can label. Pet food cans: Pet food containers made out of alumunim that are empty, clean, and dry can be recycled, even if they are small.
fields.Garbage: If an aluminum can has a removable plastic lid, the lid can go in the garbage, but the can should go in the recycling.
fields.Didyouknow: Using recycled aluminum to make things takes 98% less energy than using new material.

fields.Donate: Donate or resell usable bikes and parts to scrap metal dealers or community-oriented bike shops like Bike Works or Recycled Cycles .
fields.Recycling: Clean metal bike parts 3 inches or larger can go in the recycling: Items must fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits for your cart.
fields.Garbage: Worn tires, broken inner tubes, and Bike parts smaller than 3 inches go in the garbage.
fields.Transferstation: Drop off small metal parts and loose bike chains in scrap metal bins for recycling. Bring bikes and parts to city transfer stations to be recycled. No fee.

fields.Garbage: Put all blister packages in the garbage. They aren't recyclable. Blister packages are the clear hard-to-open plastic packaging from items such as batteries, toys, and small electronics.

fields.Recycling: Small plastic bottle caps if screwed onto an empty plastic bottle can be put into the recycling Loose plastic and metal lids 3 inches in diameter or larger
fields.Garbage: Loose lids of any material less than 3 inches in diameter Loose plastic bottle caps less than 3 inches in diameter Metal beer and soda caps less than 3 inches in diameter
fields.Transferstation: Put small metal caps, such as beer and soda caps, in a metal can or container so they are not loose and drop off in scrap metal bin at the Transfer Stations.
fields.Didyouknow: Rule of Thumb: If the container and lid are made of different materials, such as a glass jar with a metal lid, always seperate them and dispose of accordingly. Plastic lids can always be recycled when screwed onto a plastic bottle.

fields.Hazardous: Bring fluids to a household hazardous waste facility . Fees may apply. Don't mix fluids together! Put fluids in a sealed container that is 5 gallons or less. Limit 50 gallons per trip
fields.Didyouknow: Don't pour brake and transmission fluids down drains or toilets, down storm drains, or into soil. These all cause water pollution.

fields.Garbage: Plastic bread bags go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: These plastic food bags often contain food residue and moisture that can contaminate recycling.

fields.Donate: You can donate bricks in good condition to many building supply stores which specialize in salvaged materials.
fields.Garbage: Brick can go in the garbage if it doesn't exceed the weight limits for your cart size.
fields.Transferstation: Transfer station fees apply.

fields.Recycling: Pieces of broken bottles and jars 3 inches or larger
fields.Garbage: All pieces of broken drinking glasses or wine glasses Pieces of broken bottles and jars smaller than 3 inches All broken kitchenware glass or baking glass such as Pyrex All broken frosted glass Broken aquarium glass
fields.Didyouknow: Food and beverage glass jars and bottles have a different melting point than other types of glass, which is why they are recyclable and other glass is not.

fields.Recycling: Clean buckets and carts go in your curbside recycling cart or can be set at the curb next to your cart.
Clean butter boxes and other clean paper food boxes go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: All butter wrappers go in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Soup and other food cans when they are empty, clean and dry. Keep can lids partially attached or push the lid into the can. You don't need to remove the can label. Recycle when the can and lid are clean, empty and dry. Alternatively, the loose can lid can be put into the can and the top crimped to keep the lid inside.
fields.Garbage: Loose can lids (not attached) go in the garbage. Rusty cans go in the garbage. Cans that are not empty, clean and dry go in the garbage.

fields.Donate: You can melt leftover wax by placing the candle glass in hot water. Then pour the candle wax into another candle. You may need a new wick to light the new candle. You can also repurpose candle glass or metal tins for different uses such as drinking cups or storage devices.
fields.Recycling: Metal candle containers can be recycled if the container tin is empty, clean, and dry, and the containers are three inches or greater in diameter. Candle wax and candle glass are not recyclable.
fields.Garbage: Candle wax and candle glass go in the garbage. Candle wax and candle glass are not recyclable. Some candle glass is made from heat-treated glass. This is a different type of glass than bottle or jar glass that is recyclable. Mixing heat-treated glass with bottle or jar glass during the recycling process can cause the entire collection to be contaminated and no longer recyclable. Tealights, incense, oil wicks, and other accessories go in the garbage.

fields.General: Batteries are NOT allowed in the garbage, see below for disposal guidance and rules Lead acid vehicle batteries, such as from cars, RVs, boats or golf carts. Follow these links for guidance on Household Batteries , Embedded Batteries or E-Mobility Batteries .
fields.Transferstation: Bring vehicle batteries to a city transfer station where the materials will be reclaimed and recycled. No fee. Limit of 5 car batteries per visit.
fields.Dropoff: Bring batteries to a city household hazardous waste facility , where the materials will be reclaimed and recycled. No fee. Remove batteries from vehicles. Limit 5 lead-acid auto or maine batteries per visit (batteries from electric vehicles are not accepted).
fields.Hazardous: Batteries cannot go in the garbage because they contain chemicals that are harmful to people, animals, and the environment. Learn more about the city of Seattle's Ban on Batteries and Electronics in Garbage .

fields.General: Includes containers with silver lining such as snack jars and bags, coffee containers, chip canisters, or foil lined cartons used in grocery delivery.
fields.Recycling: Plastic lids 3 inches in diameter or larger
fields.Garbage: Nut, chip, frozen juice and coffee canisters Plastic lids less than 3 inches in diameter
fields.Didyouknow: Foil- and metal-lined containers and canisters go in the garbage because the foil lining cannot be separated from the other materials.

fields.General: It is okay to leave small amounts of tape, labels, and staples attached to cardboard. Remove excessive amounts before recycling. For large cardboard that will not fit in your recycle container— Put extra recycling in a personal can, paper bag, or box up to 96 gallons (same size as the cart) next to the cart on collection day.
fields.Recycling: Cardboard and flattened cardboard boxes go in the recycling. You can leave labels and tape on the boxes. Remove any packing materials inside and dispose of properly. Pet scratch pads made of cardboard are recyclable.
fields.Foodandyard: Cardboard with grease or oil stains (like pizza boxes) go in the food and yard waste cart. Put cardboard that is mostly wet in the food and yard waste cart.
fields.Garbage: Waxed cardboard like produce boxes goes in the garbage.
fields.Binside: Cardboard that doesn't fit can go next to your cart on your recycling day. Bundle and set next to the cart, or put in a box or container next to your cart. Remove foam and packing materials. There is no charge for extra recycling.

fields.Donate: Donate area rugs in good condition to thrift or through reuse community groups. Contact thrifts stores to confirm they will accept area rugs.
fields.Garbage: Fees apply. Carpet and padding can go in the garbage. Cut into smaller pieces if carpet or padding doesn't fit in your cart with the lid closed. Coir mats go in the garbage.
fields.Curbside: Call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000 to request special item pickup . Fees apply.
fields.Transferstation: Bring carpet and padding up to 8 feet long and 200 pounds to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check the rates page.

fields.Recycling: Rusted metal can be recycled unless the metal is falling apart. Small amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber can be attached.
fields.Garbage: Metal items with large amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber attached Metal items that are smaller than 3 inches
fields.Curbside: Submit a request online or call (206) 684-3000 to schedule a bulky item for large pieces pickup. Fee applies.
fields.Hazardous: All metal, except car parts, is accepted as recycling at city transfer stations . There is no charge for recycling at the transfer station. Maximum size is 8 feet long. There is a charge for appliances, limit 2 per load.
fields.Binside: Large metal parts can be put at the curb for pickup on your recycling collection day. These must be bundled or tied. The maximum size is 2 feet on all sides.

fields.Garbage: CD and DVD cases go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Stores that sell used CDs or DVDs may take cases in good condition.
fields.Didyouknow: CD and DVD cases are made out of plastics that are not accepted for recycling.

aliases: CDs, DVDs, Records, Video Tapes, and Floppy Disks

fields.Donate: Donate CDs, DVDs, records, and video tapes in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give away usable CDs and DVDs through sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing . You may also be able to sell records or CDs to your local record store!
fields.Recycling: The cardboard sleeve of vinyl records is recyclable.
fields.Garbage: CDs DVDs Floppy discs CD and DVD cases Video tapes Records Vinyl records
fields.Didyouknow: The plastic and metal from CDs and DVDs are not accepted for recycling.

fields.Recycling: Clean and Empty cereal and cracker boxes go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Plastic liners and trays from food boxes go in the garbage.

fields.Donate: Donate car seats in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Garbage: Old and expired child car seats go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Don't reuse broken car seats or car seats that have been in accidents. It isn't safe.

fields.Garbage: Chip bags go in the garbage because they are made from several different materials that can't be separated for recycling.

fields.General: Sandpaper is not recyclable.
fields.Recycling: Office paper, printer paper, and plain paper folders go in the recycling. No need to remove staples. Remove large metal pieces before recycling, such as on hanging file folders.
fields.Garbage: Paper scraps and cards smaller than 3 inches Wet or soiled paper Sandpaper, used or unused Paper with paint, glitter, decorations, glue, etc. goes in the garbage Loose staples are garbage, they are too small to be recycled Laminated paper, and other paper items made of two or more materials that cannot be separated

fields.General: Free disposal from December 26 to January 31. Remove ALL decorations, flocking, or wiring from trees, wreaths, and greens. Starting February 1st, regular fees apply.
fields.Foodandyard: Place up to two completely undecorated and unflocked trees and/or holiday greens without decorations or soil, next to your cart on collection day for free from December 26 through January 31. Trees must be cut to 4-foot lengths and the trunk diameter should not exceed 4 inches. Starting February 1, extra yard waste fee applies
fields.Garbage: Artificial plastic trees, wreaths, and garlands can be put in the garbage. Make sure not to exceed weight limits for your cart size. Avoid extra charges: the lid on your cart should close completely.
fields.Transferstation: From December 26 to January 31, bring Christmas trees to a city transfer station for free. Starting February 1, regular fees apply. Remove all decorations, tree flocking, and wiring Trees cannot exceed 8 feet in length Trunks cannot exceed 4 inches in diameter Stations will accept up to 3 trees per vehicle
fields.Binside: From December 26 to January 31, holiday trees, wreaths, and greens without decorations can be composted for free. Place on the curb next to your food and yard waste cart on your regular collection day. Flocked and plastic trees or wreaths will be charged as extra garbage Remove all decorations: lights, tinsel, metal clips, ornaments, and bows Trees must be cut into lengths to 4-feet or shorter For bundling branches, use sisal string or twine (not plastic) At apartments, two trees may be placed next to each food and yard waste cart at no extra charge each collection day. Each additional tree will be picked up as extra yard waste ( fees apply ).

fields.General: If you are a construction business with large quantities of construction material waste, please see Seattle's Construction and Demolition page.
fields.Donate: Many construction materials are salvageable. Check the Salvage Building Materials page to find more information about what materials can be saved.
fields.Foodandyard: Clean, untreated and unpainted wood goes in the food and yard waste cart. All pieces must be 4 inches or less in diameter and 4 feet or less in length. Put sawdust or shavings in paper bags or boxes to keep from scattering. Avoid extra charges -- Items should fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Transferstation: Bring untreated wood waste to city transfer stations . All pieces must be 4 feet or less in length and 4 inches or less in diameter. Nails and staples are okay.
fields.Dropoff: Check the King County What Do I Do With tool to find locations that will take clean wood for repurposing or recycling.
fields.Didyouknow: Compost processing equipment removes metal staples and nails. However, the equipment can't remove plastic.
fields.Binside: Bundles can be set next to the cart. Fees apply. Check rates here . Tie bundles with natural twine. No plastic allowed. Bundles must be 2 feet or less in diameter.

fields.Recycling: Empty non-toxic cleaning supply containers go in the recycling. Empty and rinsed bleach, drain cleaner, and other cleaners bottles go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Non toxic chemicals, such as soaps and detergents can go in the garbage. All cleaning wipes with or without cleaner, as well as paper towels used to wipe cleaning products, go in the garbage.
fields.Hazardous: Bring partially used cleaning supplies to a household hazardous waste facility for free drop off.

fields.Donate: Donate gently used clothing to a local thrift store .
fields.Garbage: Clothes and shoes can go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Stained, worn out, ripped, or damaged clothing and shoes can be turned into new products through Threadcycle . Some local thrift and second-hand stores are partners and will accept these items at their regular collection or drop box locations.

fields.Garbage: Empty CO2 chargers under 2 pounds go in the garbage.

fields.Foodandyard: Paper coffee filters are compostable and go in the food and yard waste together with coffee grounds.
fields.Garbage: Plastic, plastic-coated, or cloth coffee filters go in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Clean, Empty and Dry coffee pods larger than 3 inches in diameter.
fields.Foodandyard: Coffee pods are compostable if they are labelled compostable and there is an accompanying certification from BPI, CMA, or TUV. Aluminum Nespresso pods can be recycled at Nespresso stores or mailed back to Nespresso. For details, see the Nespresso website .
fields.Garbage: Coffee pods smaller than 3 inches. Wrappers should go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: The vast majority of coffee pods are less than 3 inches in diameter, and not recyclable. Even if they are labeled as 'Recyclable'.

fields.Donate: Many household materials in good condition are salvageable. Check the Salvage Building Materials page and the Northwest Building Salvage Network to find more information about what materials can be salvaged and reused.
fields.Garbage: Wood paneling and composite materials can go in the garbage: Break paneling down so it fits in your cart with the lid closed. Make sure it doesn't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Curbside: Schedule a Special Item Pickup online or call (206)684-3000. Fees apply.
fields.Transferstation: Bring wood paneling and composite materials to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check rates here.
fields.Binside: Paneling that does not fit in your cart with the lid closed can be put in a plastic bag and set next to your garbage cart as EXTRA garbage on collection day. Fees apply. Check rates here.

fields.Foodandyard: Bags labeled "Compostable" from approved brands go in the food and yard waste. Approved compostable plastic bags are green or brown tinted and are clearly labeled ‘Compostable’. Look for certification marks from brands such as “BPI”, TÜV, or CMA.
fields.Garbage: Bags that aren't from approved brands or do not say 'Compostable' on them go in the garbage. Biodegradable bags are not compostable, and go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Usually green bags are compostable, but not always. Check to make sure that the green bag also says "compostable" and is an approved brand. For more information about compostable labeling requirements, visit the Department of Ecology's website .

fields.Foodandyard: Items labeled “Compostable,” and have a certification mark such as BPI, TÜV, or CMA, go in the food and yard waste. Compostable food service packaging items may include: Clamshell-style, hinge-lid paper fiber To-Go food containers Fold-top To-Go paper boxes Cups Plates Straws and utensils Portion cups Paper napkins Paper towels Uncoated (not shiny) paper plates and bowls (such as Chinet brand) Sugar packets Learn more about compostable packaging (PDF).
fields.Garbage: Plastic stickers or labels must be removed from compostable food packaging before going in the compost cart. How to identify plastic stickers and labels: harder to tear elastic or stretch when attempting to remove shiny cannot see fibers when cut
fields.Didyouknow: Some compostable food containers look and feel almost identical to non-compostable containers. Always check the labeling to find out. Compostable straws are usually brown, and are more rigid than plastic straws.

fields.General: If you are a construction business with large quantities of construction material waste, please see Seattle's Construction and Demolition page.
fields.Donate: Many construction materials are salvageable. Check the Salvage Building Materials page to find more information about what materials can be saved.
fields.Garbage: Concrete and asphalt can go in the garbage if it doesn't exceed the weight limits , and fits in your cart with the lid closed. Each concrete or asphalt piece must be less than 2 cubic feet.
fields.Transferstation: Bring concrete and asphalt to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check rates here. Each concrete or asphalt piece must be less than 2' x 2' x 2' and less than 200 lbs.
fields.Dropoff: Check the King County What Do I Do With tool to find locations that will take concrete or asphalt for recycling.

fields.Recycling: Metal food containers like oil jugs or cookie tins are recyclable if they are empty, clean, and dry.
Metal parts larger than 3 inches go in the recycling. Small amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber can be attached.
fields.Garbage: Metal items with large amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber attached Metal items that are smaller than 3 inches
fields.Curbside: For large items: Submit a request online or call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000 to request bulky item collection. Fees apply.
fields.Hazardous: All metal, except car parts, is accepted as recycling at city transfer stations . There is no fee for most metal. Maximum size is 8 feet long. There is a charge for appliances, limit 2 per load.
fields.Binside: Large metal parts can be put at the curb for pickup on your recycling collection day. These must be bundled or tied. The maximum size is 2 feet on all sides.

fields.Garbage: Corks, both natural and synthetic (including those made out of sugarcane), go in the garbage. Natural corks are too dense to compost. Synthetic corks are made of various materials and are not recyclable.
fields.Dropoff: Corks can be dropped off for recycling at a handful of locations across Seattle via ReCORK .

fields.General: Receipts can be made from many different materials. The kind of reciept you have determines where it should go. The most common reciepts (from most stores) are coated in chemicals and not recyclable.
fields.Recycling: Receipts that are made of uncoated paper are recyclable. These are usually white or yellow, and are crisp and not shiny. You might receive a receipt like this from an antique store or yard sale.
fields.Foodandyard: Paper receipts that have grease stains from food can go in the compost container. Note that greasy coated receipts should never go in the compost, only garbage.
fields.Garbage: The most common type of receipt, (coated/thermal,) always goes in the garbage. This is what you will commonly recieve from automatic printers at stores.
fields.Didyouknow: Reciept paper has a chemical coating on it that make it non recyclable.

fields.Recycling: Cardboard and flattened cardboard boxes go in the recycling. Remove all packing materials from boxes.
fields.Foodandyard: Cardboard with grease or oil stains (like pizza boxes) go in the food and yard waste cart. Put cardboard that is mostly wet in the food and yard waste cart. Remove all labels and tape.
fields.Binside: Cardboard that doesn't fit can go next to your cart on your recycling day. There is no charge for extra recycling. Bundle and set next to the cart, or put in a box or container next to your cart.

fields.Garbage: Dead animals weighing less than 15 pounds should be double-bagged and placed in your garbage can.
fields.Caution: Dead animals weighing more than 15 pounds need to be picked up by animal control . Please call (206)-386-7387.

aliases: Deli, Coffee, or Soft Drink Lids

fields.Recycling: Lids 3 inches in diameter or larger go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Lids less than 3 inches in diameter go in the garbage.

Small amounts of dirt, soil, mud, or sand, including those contaminated with non-hazardous materials such as plastic, metal, and glass, can go in the garbage. Be careful not to exceed weight limits for your cart. Do not put dirt, soil, mud, or sand in the food and yard waste cart, as it can harm the composting process.
fields.Transferstation: Dirt or soil contaminated with non-hazardous materials such as metal, plastic, or glass can be brought to city transfer stations . Check rates here .
fields.Dropoff: Larger amounts of clean dirt, soil, mud, or sand (free of trash and contamination) can be recycled by various landscaping supply companies in the area.
fields.Hazardous: Contaminated soil (oil, fuel, heavy metals, etc.) must to be diposed of through an approved vendor. Go to HazWasteHelp.org for more information.

fields.Garbage: Put all disposable (even if marked "compostable") diapers in a bag, tie off, and place in garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Diapers, no matter if they are made of commercially compostable materials or not, are not accepted in our curbside food and yard waste service. It’s not the diapers themselves that are a problem, it’s the contents inside of them. Human waste is not accepted in our food and yard waste collection because it has the potential to spread harmful pathogens and diseases into the compost that can be used to grow food. For this reason, we ask that you please put compostable diapers in the garbage.

fields.Garbage: Drinking glasses can go in the garbage, whether they're broken or not.
fields.Didyouknow: Drinking glasses can't be recycled because they have different melting points than glass bottles and jars that recyclers can process.

fields.Garbage: Dryer sheets go in the garbage. They are made from polyester substrate and can't be recycled or composted. Lint goes in the garbage. It is not recyclable nor compostable.

fields.General: If you are a construction business with large quantities of construction material waste, please see Seattle's Construction and Demolition page.
fields.Donate: Many household materials in good condition are salvageable. Check the Salvage Building Materials page and the Northwest Building Salvage Network to find more information about what materials can be salvaged and reused.
fields.Garbage: Home plastic plumbing, insulation, tar paper, caulking, silicone and wall material is garbage. Insulation material must be bagged. Garbage container lids must be able to close. Containers cannot exceed their weight limit .
fields.Transferstation: Construction material can be dropped off at one of Seattle's Transfer Stations for disposal. Fees apply.
fields.Dropoff: Check the King County What Do I Do With tool to find locations that will take building materials such as clean drywall and fiberglass .
Many scrap metal dealers will buy asbestos-free metal duct, fireplace inserts and furnace/stove/chimney parts.
fields.Hazardous: To dispose of duct work, fire place inserts, or other materials - that contains asbestos, find disposal sites on the Puget Sound Clean Air Agency or call them at (206) 343-8800.
fields.Didyouknow: Duct work, fireplace inserts and furnace parts are not accepted at city transfer stations.

fields.Recycling: Rigid plastic egg cartons that are empty, clean, and dry.
fields.Foodandyard: Paper egg cartons are not a highly valuable recyclable; therefore, it is best to place them in the Food and Yard Waste container for composting.
fields.Garbage: Foam egg cartons are not recyclable nor compostable.
fields.Didyouknow: Many egg sellers at farmers markets will take back clean egg cartons to reuse them.

fields.Garbage: Car parts 3 inches or smaller on any side can go in the garbage. Car part accessories like windshield wipers or floor mats go in the garbage. Snow chains should go in the garbage unless they are in good condition and can be donated.
fields.Dropoff: Many scrap metal dealers will buy car parts.
fields.Didyouknow: Car parts aren't accepted for recycling because they contain grease, which contaminates other recyclable items.

fields.Recycling: Recycle all paper envelopes, including those with plastic windows.
fields.Garbage: Bubble pack, plastic, and mixed material envelopes go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: This recyclable item is banned from Seattle's garbage.

fields.Donate: Donate electronic equipment in working condition to local thrift stores or resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Curbside: Submit a request online or call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000 to schedule a Special Item pickup. Fees apply.
fields.Dropoff: King County’s Take It Back Network is a network of e-cyclers that accept a variety of electronic equipment. Use their search tool to find the closest location to you. No fee for TVs, monitors, and computers covered from households and small businesses through the E-Cycle Washington program. Fees may apply for other items. 1-800-RECYCLE is both a hotline and an online tool that connects you or your business to recycling services across Washington. fields.Hazardous: E-Waste can't go in the garbage because they contain materials harmful to people, animals, and the environment.
fields.Didyouknow: Electronics can't go in the garbage because they contain materials harmful to people, animals, and the environment.

fields.Donate: Contact your local thrift store to see if they take prescription glasses in good condition.
fields.Garbage: Eyeglasses can go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: You can donate eyeglasses to The Lions Club or check to see if where you got your glasses has a take back program.

fields.Donate: Donate fabrics and textiles to thrift stores. Including stained, worn out, ripped, or damaged fabric or textiles can be turned into new products through Threadcycle . Some local thrift and second-hand stores are partners and will accept these items at their regular collection or drop box locations. Donate plastic shower curtains in good condition to local thrift stores.
fields.Foodandyard: 100% authentic, natural burlap (made from plant fibers, not polyester) is compostable. Cut it into strips and place in compost.
fields.Garbage: Fabric and textiles can go in the garbage. Electric blankets, denim insulation, and cotton insulation go in the garbage, they are not able to be recycled through Threadcycle. Plastic shower curtains go in the garbage.

fields.General: For additional info regarding Fats, Oils, or Grease
fields.Recycling: You can recycle up to 2 gallons of cooking oil on each recycling collection day: Only cooking oil that is liquid at room temperature is recyclable. Pour cooled oil into a 1-gallon plastic container with a tight-fitting, screw-on lid. Set up to 2 labeled 1-gallon containers on the curb next to your recycling cart. Apartment / Condo residents: Set out up to 2 labeled 1-gallon containers per cart at your building/complex.
fields.Foodandyard: Small amounts of oil and grease can be wiped up by paper towels or newspaper and placed in the food and yard waste container (compost).
fields.Garbage: Put cooled fats, oil, or grease in a closed container, Ziploc bag, or in a thick plastic bag that's tightly tied.
fields.Didyouknow: Fats, oils, and grease shouldn't be poured down the drain because they clog pipes and create backups.
fields.Binside: You can recycle up to 2 gallons of cooking oil on each recycling collection day: Pour cooled oil into a 1-gallon plastic container with a tight-fitting, screw-on lid. Label the container with your name and address. Set up to 2 labeled 1-gallon containers on the curb next to your recycling cart. Apartment / Condo residents: Set out up to 2 labeled 1-gallon containers per cart at your building/complex.

fields.Donate: Bring fiberglass to city transfer stations . Fees apply.
fields.Garbage: Fiberglass can go in the garbage: Items must fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Caution: Fiberglass can irritate your skin and eyes. Wear gloves, googles, and protective clothing when handling.

fields.Garbage: Empty CO2 and halon (bromo difluoromethane) fire extinguishers go in the garbage.
fields.Hazardous: Bring fire extinguishers that are full or partially full to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee.

fields.Garbage: BBQ briqettes and fireplace and briquette ashes must be completely cooled, wetted, and placed in a closed box or bag. This prevents ash from scattering when your garbage is collected.

Only fireworks that are completely burned out AND cooled down by submerging them in a bucket of water for fifteen minutes can be put in the garbage. DO NOT put used fireworks that haven't been soaked into a paper or plastic bag, or unused fireworks in the garbage. This could catch fire in the bag. If disposed of improperly, used fireworks can pose a danger to employees who handle trash at local transfer stations.
fields.Hazardous: Call the Seattle Police Firing Range at (206) 684-7470 to dispose of small, unused residential fireworks.

Bring up to 10 flares per trip to a household hazardous waste facility for no fee. Some limits may apply. Call the King County Hazardous Waste Help Line at (206) 296-4692 for more information before dropping off your flares.

fields.Garbage: Incandescent, LED, Halogen, LED commercial downlights and Xenon light bulbs go in the garbage.
fields.Curbside: For Compact Fluorescent bulbs ONLY: Submit a request online or call (206) 684-3000 to schedule a pickup for a $5 fee.
fields.Hazardous: Bring up to 10 fluorescent tubes and CFLs per trip to a household hazardous waste facility or to a LightRecycle location. No fee.
fields.Didyouknow: Fluorescent tubes and CFLs are banned from the garbage because they contain mercury, which is highly toxic. To prevent breaking the tubes or bulbs and releasing mercury when storing or transporting, wrap them in newspaper or put back in their original packaging. Halogen and xenon light bulbs can't be recycled because they have different melting points than recyclable glass bottles and jars.

fields.Garbage: Baby wipes, wet wipes, cleaning wipes, and any wipes labeled "flushable" go in your garbage. If flushed down your toilet, they can clog your sewer pipes. Single use wipes labelled as compostable should still go in the garbage, as Seattle only accepts compostable serviceware outside of organics.
fields.Didyouknow: All wipes go in the garbage and not in the toilet or in the compost, regardless of what their packaging says. Paper towels that have only been used to dry hands after washing are the only similar type of material accepted in the compost.

fields.Garbage: Foamcore and foam boards go in the garbage.
Plastic liners, bags, waxed bags, and trays from food boxes, such as cereal or crackers, go in the garbage.

fields.General: Any unwanted food product goes in the compost! Snacks, leftovers, spoiled food, meat and dairy-- it's all acceptable! Learn more about food waste reduction and composting here . Make sure to remove any sort of plastic from your food scraps, like produce stickers! Plastic does not decompose and is extremely hard to sort out in the compost process. It will then be in the final product compost and sold to customers. If there is plastic in the compost, that means we are putting plastics and microplastics into our gardens and soil.
fields.Foodandyard: Fruit and vegetables (including pits and seeds) Bread, pasta, rice, and grains (cooked and uncooked) Eggshells and nutshells Coffee grounds, filters, and tea bags Meat, fish, and chicken Dairy products like milk, butter, and cheese Flour, sugar Protein powder Bones and seafood shells Compostable (uncoated) paper such as paper napkins, paper towels, and pizza boxes Spoiled or moldy food
fields.Garbage: Tea bags that are made of plastic go in the garbage
fields.Didyouknow: The shiny coating on paper plates and cups is usually plastic. Scrape the coating with your fingernail or a knife. If wax collects under your fingernail, the coating is wax. Wax-coated cups and plates can go in your food waste cart.

fields.Foodandyard: Uncoated paper with food or grease on it goes in the food and yard waste. This includes: Pizza boxes Paper napkins Paper towels used to wipe up food Uncoated (not shiny) paper plates and bowls (such as Chinet brand) compostable straws and utensils wet newspaper
fields.Garbage: Shiny, plastic-coated food packaging and fast food wrappers, paper plates, or bowls go in the garbage. Butcher paper and aluminum foil food wrappers belong in the garbage. They are made of multiple materials and are hard to properly clean for recycling.
fields.Didyouknow: The shiny coating on paper plates and cups is usually plastic. Scrape the coating with your fingernail or a knife. If wax collects under your fingernail, the coating is wax. Wax-coated cups and plates can go in your food waste cart.

fields.Recycling: Clean frozen food boxes and other food boxes Clean, empty and dry trays that hold the food Plastic coated cardboard and paperboard
fields.Garbage: Food trays that are not clean empty and dry go in the garbage.

fields.Hazardous: To dispose furnaces, furnace parts, or boilers that contain asbestos, contact the Puget Sound Clean Air Agency at (206) 343-8800.
fields.Didyouknow: Many scrap metal dealers will buy asbestos-free metal duct and furnace parts.

fields.Donate: Resell or give away a gently used hose using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing . You could also consider contacting your local P-patch community garden to donate a gently used hose.
fields.Garbage: Hoses go in the garbage. Cut hose into pieces if it doesn't fit in your cart with the lid closed.
fields.Didyouknow: Old garden hoses can be repurposed to pad ropes used to support new or weak trees.

fields.General: For information about compressed fuel containers, See Small Gas Containers .
fields.Garbage: Empty fuel cans that are 5 gallons or smaller can go in the garbage. Leave lid off empty can for 2 days before putting in garbage to release fuel fumes.
fields.Hazardous: Small fuel canisters (5 gallons or less) with any amount of gas, diesel, kerosene, butane or other fuel can be taken to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee.
Bring fuel to a household hazardous waste facility : Put fuel in a sealed container that is 5 gallons or less. Use fuel-compatible containers (not food or milk jugs). Limit 30 gallons per trip.

fields.Garbage: Gel hot and cold packs go in the garbage. They are not recyclable or compostable. Gel packs labeled 'Compostable' are not accepted in food and yard Waste carts. Do Not pour gel down the drain or flush down the toilet. It will clog the pipes.

fields.General: Plastic gift wrap, soiled wrapping paper and wrapping paper with excess glitter, tape, paint and metallic coatings go into the garbage.
fields.Recycling: Wrapping paper Paper gift bags Paper gift boxes Gift tissue paper Kraft Paper Construction Paper Inner cardboard tube Clean, and dry wrapping paper go into recycling.
fields.Garbage: These items go in the garbage: Plastic gift wrap Foil gift wrap Plastic or foil gift bows Plastic gift bags

fields.Recycling: Glass bottles and jars larger than 3 inches. Lids 3 inches or larger
fields.Garbage: Bottles smaller than three inches, any frosted glass bottles, Pyrex, and any heat-treated bakeware or kitchen glass is not recyclable.
fields.Didyouknow: Jars coated with oily food like peanut butter can be wiped first with a paper towel (put the paper towel in the food and yard waste). Very small amounts of peanut butter or food residue are okay.

fields.Donate: Donate glass or ceramic household items in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Garbage: Damaged glass or ceramic household items such as plates, bowls, drinking glasses, or terra cotta pots can go in the garbage. Any frosted glass, picture frame glass, glass used for candles, heat-treated bakeware or kitchen glass is garbage. These types of glass are not recyclable
fields.Didyouknow: Glass other than jars and bottles can't be recycled because they have different melting points than jars and bottles, which is the glass that recyclers process.

fields.Garbage: Non-toxic glues go in the garbage. This includes Elmer's, glue sticks, and other glues used in schools.
fields.Hazardous: Bring glues and adhesives labeled with caution , warning , danger , or poison to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee. All containers must be 5 gallons or less. Limit 50 gallons per trip.

fields.Garbage: You can put gold, silver, and other precious metals in the garbage. It is not a material that can be collected in large enough amouts for recycling.
fields.Dropoff: You can often sell gold, silver, and broken jewelry to jewelry buyers or coin and precious metal dealers.

fields.General: Vehicles such as cars, trucks, vans, SUVs, recreational vehicles (RVs), campers, and golf carts can be recycled, removed, and reported using the resources below. If you are the vehicle owner: Check online for non-profits that accept working or non-working vehicles and RVs. These generally require title free and clear of liens. Some organizations will remove with no cost to the owner. Pay for service: There are many businesses in Seattle that can be found online to remove unwanted vehicles and dispose and/or recycle for a fee Abandoned Vehicles Report abandoned vehicles to one of the below for removal. Find It, Fix It tool If on private property , contact Seattle Junk Vehicle Program at 296-684-8940 or by email at SPUGIU@seattle.gov If on public property (alongside the road or road right of way), contact City of Seattle Abandoned Vehicle Hotline at 206-684-8763 or on the SDOT website .
fields.Dropoff: Many charitable organizations accept vehicles and provide a receipt for a tax deduction.

fields.Foodandyard: Grass clippings and small amounts of sod can go in the food and yard waste. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Dropoff: Bring large amounts of grass clippings and sod to city transfer stations . Fees apply.

fields.Recycling: Greeting cards and other paper cards go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Cards with lots of plastic, glitter, or other materials: remove the non-paper parts and put in the garbage.

fields.Donate: Reuse bags in good condition
fields.Recycling: Clean and dry paper bags
fields.Foodandyard: Paper bags that are wet or food-soiled

fields.Transferstation: Bring gutters 8 feet or less in length to city transfer stations : Fees apply for plastic gutters. There is no fee for aluminum gutters.

fields.Donate: Donate hand tools in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Recycling: Mainly metal tools 3 inches or more in size Can include small amounts of wood, rubber, or plastic
fields.Garbage: Metal tools less than 3 inches Tools that contain large amounts of rubber, wood, or plastic

fields.Garbage: Intact (with cover and binding) hardcover books go in the garbage. This is because the hard cover and binding are not recyclable.
fields.Didyouknow: Hardcover books can't be recycled due to the glue in the binding.

fields.Garbage: Empty helium tanks 5 gallons or smaller can go in the garbage: Turn the valve all the way to the left to release remaining helium. Avoid extra charges: Tank should fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Dropoff: Check with your supplier for return and refill options. For tanks larger than 5 gallons or commercial cylinders, refer to information printed on the tank for instructions on recycling or exchange options.

fields.Garbage: Empty hobby chemical containers go in the garbage.
fields.Hazardous: Bring partially full containers of hobby chemicals labeled with caution , warning , danger , or poison to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee. All containers must be 5 gallons or less. Limit 50 gallons per trip.

fields.Donate: Donate holiday lights in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Garbage: String/Holiday lights can go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Check King County's Green Holiday website for drop off locations for holiday light recycling options. You can drop off your solar garden lights at EcoLight for recycling.

fields.General: Hot or cold to-go cups can be recycled it they are empty clean and dry.
fields.Recycling: Empty and dry paper cups. Paper cup sleeves go into recycling. Plastic to-go cups
fields.Foodandyard: Hot or coffee cups labeled as "Compostable" Some plastic-looking to-go cups may be compostable! Look for the word "compostable" and a certification.
fields.Garbage: Styrofoam coffee cups Non-compostable paper cups stained with liquid Non-paper cup sleeves Plastic straws

fields.Foodandyard: Houseplants go in the food and yard waste. Remove plants from potting soil and planters.
fields.Transferstation: Houseplants can go to city transfer stations as yard waste. Remove soil and pots. Fees apply. Check rates here .

fields.Donate: Donate furniture in good condition to local thrift stores . Resell or give away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing . Unwanted light fixtures or other household wares in working condition can be donated to salvage stores. Learn more about deconstruction and find your local salvage retailer (under reuse) on our salvage webpage .
fields.Recycling: Metal furniture frames go into recycle.
fields.Curbside: Submit a request online or call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000 to schedule a pickup. Fees apply. If you are a resident of an apartment or a condominium and do not have an SPU account, check your property manager. Furniture is not allowed in dumpsters.
fields.Transferstation: You can bring furniture and large frames to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check the rates page . If you have a piece of furniture that would fit in your garbage cart, you can dispose of it at home with you household garbage. It must fit in the cart. Do not exceed weight limits.

fields.Recycling: Plastic and Metal Ice cube trays go in the recycling if they are clean, dry, and empty.
fields.Garbage: Silicone ice cube trays go in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Metal parts larger than 3 inches go in the recycling. Small amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber can be attached. Rusted metal can be recycled unless the metal is falling apart.
fields.Garbage: Metal items with large amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber attached. Metal items that are smaller than 3 inches.
fields.Curbside: For larger items, submit a request online or call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000 to schedule a bulky item collection. Fees apply.
fields.Dropoff: All metal, except car parts, is accepted as recycling at city transfer stations . There is no fee for most metal. Maximum size is 8 feet long. There is a charge for appliances, limit 2 per load.
fields.Binside: Large metal parts can be put at the curb for pickup on your recycling collection day. These must be bundled or tied. The maximum size is 2 feet on all sides.

fields.Donate: You can donate jewelry and coins to thrift stores, and can often sell these items to jewelry buyers or coin and precious metal dealers.
fields.Garbage: You can put jewelry and coins in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: All paper junk mail goes in the recycling. Please open and separate junk mail before recycling. Items include: Catalogs Flyers Envelopes with or without clear plastic windows Newspapers Phone books Magazines Glossy paper
fields.Didyouknow: Paper and junk mail can't go in the garbage. Sign up to stop junk mail .

fields.General: For electronic key fobs, reach out to your car dealership about disposal options. Do not put them in the garbage.
fields.Garbage: Keys and other metal items smaller than 3 inches go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Small metal items can fall through the sorting machinery at the recycling plant.

fields.Garbage: Kleenex (facial tissue) goes in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Used tissues cannot be composted because they have bodily fluids on them. Do not flush tissues, as they clog pipes.

aliases: Latex Paint, acrylic paint, and water-based paint

fields.General: No type of paint should be poured down the drain. Some paints are hazardous to human health and the environment, and even non-hazardous paints can have added chemicals and metals that are difficult for our water treatment systems to filter and are harmful for our waterways.
fields.Garbage: Empty paint cans cannot be cleaned enough to recycle and should go out in the garbage. Paint cans with less than an inch of latex paint can be dried out. Paint cans with more than an inch of latex paint or with any amount of oil-based paint should be returned to a PaintCare drop-off site . Before discarding, follow these steps to safely dry out the paint can: Remove the lid and let fumes evaporate outside, away from children and animals. Separate the lid from the dried paint can and put both in the garbage. Non-architectural water-based paints or acrylic paints should be dried or absorbed with a cloth or towel and put in the garbage container. Paint brushes with dried paint go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Drop off leftover architectural paint products for free at a PaintCare drop-off site. Accepted products include latex paint, oil-based paint, stain, varnish, and more. No fee. Visit the PaintCare website to find a drop-off location near you and to view a list of accepted products.
fields.Hazardous: Bring oil-based paints and solvents like paint thinner to a Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) facility . No fee. Residential customers with unlabeled paint can bring it to a HHW facility for identification and guidance on disposal options. HHW facilities accept oil-based paints (for free) and can advise on locations to take latex paints.
fields.Didyouknow: Throwing out your dried paint can with the lid removed lets your garbage collector know that the can is empty or the paint is dried. Latex paint can be recycled into new paint! Latex paint recycling in Washington is supported by PaintCare, a state-mandated extended producer responsibility (EPR) program that requires the companies that make and sell paint to provide convenient collection, recycling, and safe management of leftover architectural paint products.

fields.Recycling: Empty and flatten laundry detergent boxes and then put in the recycling.
Plastic laundry detergent jugs that are clean, dry, and empty. Put plastic caps back onto the bottle for recycling.
fields.Garbage: Loose caps go in the garbage.

Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Transferstation: You must drain all gas, oil, and air from lawn mowers, air compressors, and other power equipment. Bring emptied mowers and equipment to city transfer stations . No charge for lawn mowers.
fields.Hazardous: Bring gas and oil to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee. Don't mix fluids together! Put fluids in a sealed container that is 5 gallons or less. Limit 50 gallons per trip.

fields.Recycling: Lead pieces 3 inches or larger can go in the recycling: Lead should fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Dropoff: Bring lead 8 feet or smaller to city transfer stations . Fees apply.

fields.Foodandyard: Leaves, seeds, and non-woody yard waste go in the food and yard waste. Items must fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart. fields.Transferstation: Bring leaves, seeds, or non-woody yard waste to city transfer stations . Fees apply .
fields.Didyouknow: Noxious weeds should be bagged and put in the garbage. Click this link to learn more!
fields.Binside: Put extra yard waste in kraft paper, labeled "compostable" bags, or bundled with natural twine for pick up on collection day. Fees apply .

fields.Dropoff: Bring license plates to a vehicle licensing office or mail them to: Department of Licensing 1125 Washington St. SE Olympia, WA 98504

fields.Curbside: Schedule a Special Item pickup online or call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000. Fees apply.
fields.Transferstation: Bring mattresses, mattress toppers and futons to city transfer stations for disposal. Fees apply. Check rates here .

fields.Recycling: Clean rigid plastic meat trays go in the recycling. Remove the plastic absorbent insert before recycling.
fields.Foodandyard: Brown or tan trays for meat, poultry, and fish are made of compostable material and go in the food and yard waste.
fields.Garbage: Any other color of foam meat tray and the plastic absorbent insert go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Brown or beige trays for meat, poultry, and fish are made from plant-based material and are compostable.

fields.Dropoff: Bring medicines to a secure medicine return site. Find locations here .
fields.Didyouknow: Always dispose of medication properly. Flushing medicine down the toilet or sink, or putting medicine in your backyard compost or food and yard waste cart can pollute our waterways and the environment.

fields.Recycling: Metal sinks and fixtures go in the recycling: They must be between 3 inches and 2 feet on all sides. Small amounts of plastic, wood, or rubber can be attached. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Curbside: Schedule a Special Item Pickup online or call SPU Customer Service at (206) 684-3000. Fees apply. Items cannot exceed 300lbs, 8 feet in height, or 4 feet in diameter.
fields.Transferstation: Bring metal sinks, tubs, and fixtures less than 8 feet on all sides to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check rates here .

fields.Foodandyard: Any leftover popcorn or kernels go in the food and yard waste.

fields.Transferstation: Bring large mirrors that don't fit in the cart to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check rates here .

fields.Foodandyard: Food-soiled bags go in the food and yard waste cart. Please remove all stickers, tape, or staples.

fields.Foodandyard: Paper napkins and towels that have food or grease on them go in the food and yard waste.

fields.Garbage: Paper towels used with cleaning products or that have bodily fluids on them and blue "shop" towels, which are made of cotton, go in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Paperback books can go in your recycling cart.

fields.Didyouknow: Find ways to avoid using pesticides from the Garden Hotline .

fields.Foodandyard: Both dry and wet pet food, dog bones, and pet treats can go in the food and yard waste. They will be turned into valuable compost.

fields.Didyouknow: Photographs aren't recyclable because of the chemicals used to create them and the short fibers used for their paper.

fields.General: Seattle doesn't recycle by number because it's not a reliable way to determine the recyclability of an item. Instead, Seattle recycles by the form that the plastic takes (e.g., rigid plastic, soft plastic). BPA plastics can be recycled if they follow the guidelines below. 1. Shape and Rigidity Plastics must be rigid enough to hold their shape during compaction in the collection trucks and during mechanical sorting at the recycling processing facility. Flimsy plastics like flexible trays found in a box of chocolates or girl scout cookie boxes are not rigid enough. These plastics are garbage. Styrofoam is not recyclable in our curbside system. Molded plastic packaging , like what batteries and other hard-to-open items are packaged in, are not recyclable. This plastic goes in the garbage. 2. Size At least three inches in diameter or at least three inches in two different directions. If a plastic is smaller than three inches, it goes in the garbage. A plastic cap that is smaller than 3 inches can remain on a plastic bottle or jug if the bottle or jug is empty, clean, and dry; and the cap does not contain any other material than plastic.

fields.General: Shredded paper should not be recycled in your recycle cart. Shredded paper acts like confetti at the recycling plant, and contaminates other recycleables. Follow the instructions below to dispose of it properly.
fields.Recycling: You may bag small amounts of shredded paper in a paper bag and keep it contained so it does not fly out and create litter. Shredded credit cards and envelopes with plastic windows are not accepted.
fields.Dropoff: The best way to dispose of shredded paper is to drop it off at a collection site to be recycled. SPU and our partners organize recycling & reuse collection events for hard-to-recycle items throughout the year, find out dates and locations . Many private companies offer shredding services, including legal offices, realtors, and some shipping companies.
fields.Didyouknow: Shredding companies and collection sites produce high volumes of shredded paper, which is baled and sold to paper mills to make new paper. Dropping off shredded paper to be recycled is the best environmental use of this material. Go paperless! Reduce the amount of paper you receive by opting to receive statements and other important documents online. Only shred paper that contains sensitive information. Check the Washington Attorney General’s website for guidelines.

fields.Foodandyard: Only straws that are labeled "Compostable" go into your food and yard waste.
fields.Garbage: Plastic straws and straws that you are unable to verify that they are approved compostable go into the garbage. Plastic straws are not recyclable.

fields.General: Foam blocks are allowed in the garbage. If you want to recycle it, there are options listed below. Foam blocks are NOT allowed in mixed recycling.
fields.Garbage: Styrofoam, polyurethane foam blocks, packing peanuts, and foam packing sheets go in the garbage. Packing peanuts must be bagged and tied closed before placing in the garbage.

fields.Dropoff: Styro Recycle in Kent accepts Styrofoam blocks, packing sheets, and packing peanuts for recycling. fields.Garbage: Foam packing sheets go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Styro Recycle in Kent accepts Styrofoam blocks, packing sheets, and packing peanuts for recycling.

fields.Garbage: Styrofoam cups go in the garbage.

fields.Foodandyard: Plastic Stickers or labels must be removed before placing in the compost container. Dirty or clean containers marked “Compostable” or “#7 PLA” (Not Shiny) Greasy pizza boxes Learn more about compostable packaging .
fields.Garbage: All Styrofoam containers Dirty plastic containers that are not marked "Compostable" or "#7 PLA" Dirty plastic-coated (shiny) paper containers
Plastic tarps go in the garbage.

fields.Hazardous: Mercury items can't go in the garbage. Bring thermometers, thermostats, and other items containing mercury to a household hazardous waste facility . No fee.
fields.Caution: Mercury can greatly harm your nervous, digestive, and respiratory systems. Don't handle mercury directly, and try to avoid breaking items that contain mercury.

fields.Transferstation: Bring up to 4 tires per visit to city transfer stations . Fees apply.

fields.Recycling: Tissue boxes go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Unused tissue goes in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Toys and sporting equipment made of metal that are 2 feet or less on all sides. Can include small amounts of attached plastic, rubber, or wood. Clean rigid plastic toys and sporting equipment 3 feet or less on all sides.
fields.Garbage: Sports equipment and toys not made of mostly rigid plastic or metal, go in the garbage. Soft plastic items like pool floaties, inflatable balls, and yoga mats go in the garbage. Unusable sports balls go into the garbage. Damaged helmets and other damaged saftey gear go into the garbage.
fields.Transferstation: Toys and sporting equipment greater than the above size limits can be taken to city transfer stations. Fees apply. Check the rates page.
fields.Caution: For battery powered toys, flashlights, and headlights, make sure to remove the batteries before disposal. Learn more about battery disposal .

fields.Foodandyard: Plants, trees, brush, and branches go in the food and yard waste: Cut down to 4 inches or less in diameter and 4 feet or less in length. Remove all soil. Pests like aphids, scale insects, etc. ok Avoid extra charges: Items should fit in your cart with the lid closed. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Transferstation: Bring plants, trees, and brush to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check the rates page. All trees, brush, or branches must be 8 feet or less in length. All pieces must be 8 inches or less in diameter.
fields.Didyouknow: You can give your plant a new home through your neighborhood Buy Nothing group or PlantAmnesty .
fields.Binside: Bundle trees and brush and set next to the cart. Fees apply. Check the rates page. Tie bundles with natural twine. No plastic allowed. Bundles must be 2 feet or less in diameter. You can put brush out in a personal plastic garbage can labeled 'Yard Waste"

fields.Garbage: Tyvek envelopes go in the garbage.

fields.Recycling: Pill bottles, such as aspirin or vitamin bottles, go in the recycling.
fields.Garbage: Clear plastic prescription medicine vials go the garbage. The plastic is too brittle to recycle.
fields.Dropoff: Bring medicines to a secure medicine return site .

fields.Garbage: Put vitamins in a closed bottle or bag and put in the garbage.

fields.Transferstation: Bring water heaters to city transfer stations : Fees apply for assembled water heaters with outer jackets and insulation intact. Check the rates page. There is no fee for water heaters with all insulation removed. To remove all insulation, the water heater must be fully dismantled and should be brought to the transfer station in pieces.

fields.Recycling: Paperboard boxes (like butter and cereal boxes) go in the recycling. They aren't true waxed cardboard. The shiny coating on these boxes is a thin layer of plastic.
fields.Garbage: Flattened waxed cardboard boxes, such as large produce boxes, go in the garbage. Modern produce and wax style boxes are plastic-coated and are not recyclable nor compostable. Receipts/receipt paper is not recyclable and goes in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Receipt paper has a chemical coating on it that makes it non-recyclable.

fields.Foodandyard: Waxed paper goes in the food and yard waste. It can't be recycled.

fields.Donate: Resell or give it away using sites like Craigslist , Freecycle , and Buy Nothing .
fields.Recycling: Individual metal blind slats go in the recycling. Remove strings, cords, and plastic and put these in the garbage.
fields.Garbage: Plastic, vinyl, and wooden blinds go in the garbage.
Windows and window glass can go in the garbage: Items must fit in your cart with the lid closed and be less than two feet by two feet. Don't exceed the weight limits printed on your cart.
fields.Transferstation: Bring windows to city transfer stations . Fees apply. Check the rates page.
fields.Didyouknow: Window glass is not accepted in the recycling containers because it melts at a different temperature than bottles and jars, which are what the glass recyclers can use.

fields.Recycling: After the foil has been removed and discarded, the wine bottle itself can be recycled.
fields.Garbage: Foil from wine bottles goes in the garbage.

fields.Donate: Donate wire clothes hangers in good condition to local thrift stores . Check with local dry cleaners. They may accept wire hangers.
fields.Garbage: Wire clothes hangers and wreath frames can go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Wire hangers and frames get tangled in the machinery at the recycling processing facility, which is why they can't be recycled.

fields.Garbage: Wires, cables, cords, and plastic can go in the garbage.
fields.Dropoff: Extension and charging cords contain recyclable metals. Check King County’s What Do I Do With tool for electronics recyclers near you. Call ahead to make sure the recycler accepts your item.
fields.Didyouknow: Wire gets tangled in the machinery at the recycling processing facility and has a plastic coating, which is why they can't be recycled.

fields.Donate: Donate wood clothes hangers in good condition to local thrift stores .
fields.Garbage: Wood clothes hangers go in the garbage.

fields.Foodandyard: Clean, untreated wood shavings, scraps, and sawdust go in the food and yard waste. Put sawdust or shavings in a closed paper bag or box to contain it.
fields.Garbage: Painted or treated wood shavings, scraps, and sawdust go in the garbage. Put sawdust and shavings in a bag and tie off.
fields.Didyouknow: Bag all garbage and loose materials for the safety of the drivers and to keep the garbage contained.

fields.Garbage: Ziploc or other plastic food bags go in the garbage.
fields.Didyouknow: Ziploc and plastic food bags contain more than one type of plastic that can't be recycled together. They also often contain food residue and moisture that contaminate recycling.

fields.Donate: Check with the brewery or restaurant to see if they will take carriers back that are in good condition. Reuse carriers if still in good condition.
fields.Recycling: Newer rigid 6-pack carriers, the type that completely cover the tops of the cans, are recyclable.
fields.Garbage: The flexible 6-pack carriers are garbage. This includes carriers for sports drinks, water bottles, and more rigid carriers for 25-ounces or 32-ounces metal beverage cans.

fields.Foodandyard: Only parchment paper that comes in a box clearly labeled as "compostable" is accepted in the food and yard compost cart. This parchment paper is coated with a natural type of silicone that is accepted in commercial compost facilities. Read the packaging carefully to be sure.
fields.Garbage: Most parchment paper is coated with a chemical or a plastic layer to give it nonstick properties. This makes it not compostable. In addition, it is not possible to recycle it because the layers can't be separated. It should be put into the garbage.
Noxious weeds (english ivy, fox tail, morning glory, knotweed, etc.) should be bagged and put in the garbage. Learn more.

fields.Recycling: Envelopes and padded envelopes that are made of only paper (no plastic) can go in your recycling bin. Cardboard envelope
fields.Garbage: At home, put plastic bag mailers/envelopes in the garbage. They are not accepted in home recycling carts. Plastic mailer Padded paper mailer/bubble wrap mailer

fields.Recycling: Cardboard boxes Paper padded mailer For more information, visit Amazon's packaging webpage .
